newsitem.title: INDIA: India's VSNL, government reach new pact.
newsitem.headline: India's VSNL, government reach new pact.

text.p: The Indian government said on Wednesday it reached a new, five-year revenue-sharing agreement with state-run telecommunications company Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL).
VSNL has a monopoly on international telecommunications services and Internet access services in India.

Under the new agreement which begins on April 1, VSNL will continue to receive net revenue of 10 rupees for every paid minute of incoming and outgoing international calls until March 31, 1999, the government said in a statement.

During the next three financial years starting on April 1, 1999, VSNL's net revenue per paid minute will be modified depending on exchange rate fluctuations and international telecommunications accounting rates, it said.
"The net revenue will be calculated based on a pre-determined formula which has been agreed between the Department of Telecommunications and VSNL," the statement said without elaborating.

The accord will subject to review if in any financial year the U.S. dollar-rupee exchange rate fluctuates by more than 10 percent in either direction or if VSNL earns less than nine rupees per minute or more than 11 rupees per minute, it said.
The license fee paid by VSNL to the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) for each international circuit will be 250,000 rupees, or about $7,000, the statement said.
The surcharge on the annual landline lease charges has been discontinued, effective on April 1, it said.

It quoted Telecom Commission chairman A.V. Gokak as saying the new agreement will give VSNL and DoT an equitable share of revenue and help both of them to make critical investments in telecommunication infrastructure.
